title: Narrow-Shell Stochasticity in Source-Sink Models of the Low Earth Orbit Environment
summary: Deterministic source-sink models are widely used to assess the long-term evolution, capacity, and sustainability of the low Earth orbit (LEO) environment. These models propagate shell-averaged populations through ordinary differential equations (ODEs), relying on individual collision, disposal, and decay events to average out within sufficiently large altitude shells. As constellation traffic is increasingly organized into kilometer- and sub-kilometer-scale shells, this averaging assumption becomes strained. We formulate the multi-shell, multi-species LEO environment as a Markov jump process…
